candidates.locator: Page 3, Section part_i, Section 3 Pathogen Control
candidates.exact_span: All sewage sludge that is applied to agricultural land, forest, a public contact site, or a reclamation site shall be treated by either the Class A or Class B pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Land-application category determines whether Class A or Class B pathogen requirements apply, which changes which numeric limits and monitoring/compliance pathways are relevant for A, which obligations attach for B, and how missing pathogen evidence is classified for C.

candidates.locator: Page 3, Section part_i, Section 3 Pathogen Control
candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge that is applied to a lawn or home garden shall be treated by the Class A pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is applied to a lawn or home garden forces Class A treatment, altering applicable limits (A), required monitoring/demonstration methods (B), and whether absent Class A evidence is a gap versus a non-applicable requirement (C).

candidates.locator: Page 3, Section part_i, Section 3 Pathogen Control
candidates.exact_span: Sewage sludge that is sold or given away in a bag shall be treated by Class A pathogen requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Bagged sludge distribution triggers mandatory Class A treatment, which changes which enforceable limits apply (A), which monitoring events are required and when (B), and how to interpret missing results for bagged product (C).

candidates.exact_span: All 6 options require either the density of fecal coliform in the sewage sludge be less than 1000 Most Probable Number (MPN) per gram of total solids (dry weight basis), or the density of Salmonella sp. bacteria in the sewage sludge be less than three MPN per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) at the time the sewage sludge is used or disposed; at the time the sewage sludge is prepared for sale or given away in a bag or other container for application to the land.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage sets alternative numeric pathogen limits, the dry-weight basis, the disjunctive fecal-coliform-or-Salmonella compliance test, and the timing of required measurements; different readings change limit applicability and exceedance findings (A), when monitoring is obligated (B), and whether a missing result corresponds to a required sampling event (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternatives 5 and 6 are not authorized to demonstrate compliance with Class A sewage sludge in Texas permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a Texas permit is in scope determines whether Alternatives 5 and 6 may be used to demonstrate Class A compliance, affecting which limits and demonstration pathways count as enforceable (A), which monitoring alternatives are permitted (B), and whether evidence gaps for those alternatives are relevant or out of scope (C).

candidates.exact_span: The pH of the sewage sludge that is used or disposed shall be raised to above 12 and shall remain above 12 for 72 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Alternative 2 imposes numeric/time-bound pH conditions for Class A demonstration; interpreting whether this alternative is selected changes applicable compliance thresholds (A), whether pH monitoring/documentation is required (B), and how absent pH records are categorized (C).

candidates.exact_span: The temperature of the sewage sludge shall be above 52 degrees Celsius for 12 hours or longer during the period that the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This temperature-duration requirement is an operative Class A alternative criterion; different interpretation of timing or measurement affects compliance evaluation (A), temperature-monitoring obligations (B), and missing-evidence handling when temperature records are absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: At the end of the 72 hour period during which the pH of the sewage sludge is above 12, the sewage sludge shall be air dried to achieve a percent solids in the sewage sludge greater than 50%.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 50% solids threshold is a numeric compliance condition for Alternative 2; how percent solids is measured or timed affects exceedance analysis (A), whether solids monitoring is required at the end of the 72-hour period (B), and whether missing solids data leaves compliance unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for enteric viruses prior to pathogen treatment. The limit for enteric viruses is one Plaque-forming Unit per four grams of total solids (dry weight basis) either before or following pathogen treatment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes both a monitoring obligation and a numeric enteric-virus limit under Alternative 3, including whether analysis may occur before or after treatment; interpretation changes required sampling (B), applicable limit values and comparison basis (A), and whether missing virus results indicate inadequate evidence versus a non-required test (C).

candidates.exact_span: The sewage sludge shall be analyzed for viable helminth ova prior
candidates.computation_change_reason: Even though the segment truncates before completing the requirement, the operative direction to analyze viable helminth ova indicates a monitoring obligation whose scope and timing must be interpreted from the surrounding Class A alternative framework, affecting whether helminth-ova monitoring was required (B) and downstream missing-evidence classification (C).
